A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynAMO research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison. Material relocated between the 43-page v1 and 52-page v2 can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimization experiments across six tasks and six backbone optimizers, with quality, diversity, computational-cost and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated comparators, secondary-objective evaluations and an initialization ablation.

M1.justification: The KL-regularized objective, source-critic constraint, dual optimization, model architectures and candidate-generation procedure are retained. The mixed-divergence extension was already present in v1 Appendix D.3. Algorithm 1's documentation edits do not establish a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.9 adds Vehicle Safety and Welded Beam evaluations, optimizing vehicle mass and beam manufacturing cost while assessing secondary safety and deflection objectives. It also evaluates GC content of candidates from the retained UTR task. The original six-task coverage remains.

E2.justification: The broader comparison adds Tri-Mentoring, ICT, PGS, Match-Opt and RGD, with results across the six original tasks and five quality/diversity metrics in v2 Tables A6–A8. These methods were absent from the corresponding v1 Tables A5–A6; existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces controlled Sobol-versus-top-k initialization comparisons using 64 initial designs, with gradient ascent except Adam for RoMA. Appendix D.9 introduces 800-design synthetic datasets and evaluates secondary-objective dispersion among 128 candidates; Welded Beam is evaluated without its original constraints. These are added protocols, not demonstrated changes to the retained experiments. The dispersion metric is inconsistently called standard deviation in the prose and variance in Table A10.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.5 and Table A14 test whether initialization explains DynAMO's diversity advantage. New Appendix D.9 and Table A10 investigate whether candidate diversity accompanies broader secondary-objective values. Existing component, hyperparameter, batch-size and oracle-budget ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and 95% confidence intervals over ten random seeds. Added tables follow that practice, and original uncertainty information remains in the relocated tables. Secondary-objective dispersion is an additional evaluation outcome, not a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for five comparators, secondary-objective exploration and paired initialization. Existing per-task scores are retained, while ranks change with the expanded comparator set: DynAMO-BO-qUCB's Best@128 average rank changes from 4.8 in v1 Table A5 to 6.3 in v2 Table A6, with its optimality gap unchanged at 20.5. This is not a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1 and its proof are substantially rewritten using a point-mass/residual decomposition and a measure-based argument. New Remark A.1 derives equivalence to KL state matching against a rescaled reference distribution. The other principal derivations and Appendix D.4 bounds are retained. The revised lemma's statement omits the optimality condition needed for its conclusion.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding contribution statements retain the same claims: DynAMO introduces distribution-matching diversity control into task- and optimizer-agnostic offline MBO while finding high-quality candidates. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting diversity to secondary-objective exploration and explaining method-dependent initialization effects. Section 7 explicitly identifies untested noisy or sparse objectives, very high-dimensional spaces and small datasets as applicability limits. The median-quality tradeoff is foregrounded and elaborated, but its basic limitation was already acknowledged in v1 Appendix D.1.

D1.justification: The added experiments document synthetic dataset sizes, dimensions, oracle sources, objective negation and initialization choices. Existing architectures, hyperparameters, hardware and code/data access statements are retained. Algorithm 1 also omits the previously explicit initialization of the critic-loop convergence variable, without explaining an implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantial coverage of first-order, evolutionary and Bayesian optimization, including a distinction between DynAMO and diversity-gated or BO-specific approaches. Appendix D.5 expands the discussion to five additional evaluated methods, and new references support the secondary-objective applications. This extends research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact. Local expansions explain optimization families and source critics, elaborate limitations, clarify Algorithm 1's inputs/comments and update publication information. The revision is principally additive rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The full main-results table becomes appendix Table A1, while main Table 1 is redesigned as a compact rank/optimality-gap summary. Expanded comparison tables are reorganized, including splitting the former diversity table, and Tables A10 and A14 display new analyses. Figure 1's legend changes from DAAG-Modified to DynAMO-Modified; existing analysis figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by testing initialization as a possible explanation for diversity gains and directly examining the proposed benefit for secondary-objective exploration, neither addressed experimentally in v1. Five additional comparators and clearer applicability limits further improve the assessment of DynAMO. These gains concern evidential credibility, not higher retained benchmark scores. The missing optimality condition in revised Lemma 3.1 and inconsistent dispersion labeling are defects, but do not outweigh the substantial empirical improvements.
